1.title: 10 Climate Zones, Varying from North to South
1.html: Alsace's vineyards form a long north–south strip, officially divided into 10 geo-climatic zones (numbered 1 to 10 from north to south), reflecting marked microclimate differences even within this small region — the basis for understanding stylistic differences between areas.
2.title: Two Key Thermal Features
2.html:
① Large temperature swings
Day–night differences can reach 15°C, helping grapes accumulate sugar while keeping natural acidity.
② Temperature inversion (Inversion des températures)
When cold air, fog and cloud settle over the Rhine plain, the hillsides at the foot of the Vosges enjoy clear, warm weather. A "warm belt" forms from mid-slope to upper-slope, 1–1.5°C warmer than the areas above and below, with gentler night cooling than on the plain — this belt usually occurs on the steepest sections, one reason why many top Grand Cru sites were chosen there.
3.title: The Vosges Rain Shadow: One of France's Driest Regions
3.html:
Alsace is not shielded from the Atlantic influence (the prevailing winds are westerly), but the Vosges mountains greatly weaken this moist air; together with northerly winds and the Foehn effect, they create Alsace's unique semi-continental climate.

600–700 mm
Average annual rainfall in Alsace
about 500–600 mm
Around Colmar (comparable to Montpellier in southern France)

Rain falls mainly in the warm season — spring and summer thunderstorms — and hail risk needs attention. This dry, sunny climate is an important foundation for Alsace's intense aromas and for its noble-rot sweet wines (VT / SGN).
4.question: Annual rainfall around Colmar is only about 500–600 mm. Which famous dry French area is it comparable to, and what causes this?
4.options.0: Comparable to Montpellier on the Mediterranean coast, because the Vosges block Atlantic westerlies, creating a rain shadow
4.options.1: Comparable to Rioja, because it sits in an inland basin
4.options.2: Comparable to Champagne, because the chalk soils drain well
4.options.3: It is a recent anomaly caused by climate change
4.explanation: Annual rainfall around Colmar is only about 500–600 mm, comparable to Montpellier on the Mediterranean coast — not because the climate is hot and dry, but because the Vosges block the moisture carried by prevailing Atlantic westerlies, creating a marked rain shadow that makes Alsace one of France's driest wine regions.
5.keyPoints.0: The region is divided into 10 climate zones (numbered 1–10 from north to south), reflecting marked microclimate differences
5.keyPoints.1: Two thermal features: day–night swings up to 15°C; temperature inversion makes hillsides warmer than the plain (warm belt +1–1.5°C)
5.keyPoints.2: The Vosges block Atlantic westerlies, making Alsace one of France's driest regions (around Colmar only about 500–600 mm, comparable to Montpellier)
5.keyPoints.3: A dry, sunny autumn climate is an important foundation for VT / SGN noble-rot sweet wines
